slides.title: Section 1 Reflections · 1.4 to 1.7
slides.notes:
§SECTION 1 REFLECTIONS · 1.4 TO 1.7

§HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:

§1. Show the slide and read the prompts aloud.
1.4 Reflection — The 3S Check: "Write the Shift, the Stake and the Step for the change you are carrying through this unit. Which of the three would your people find hardest to say back, and why?"

1.5 Reflection: "Which SCARF trigger is most frequently activated in your organisation during strategy implementation? What is the observable evidence? What counter-strategy would address the root cause?"

1.6 Reflection — The STAT Check: "Run STAT for the change you are carrying through this unit. Which element is missing for the people it affects most? What is your evidence, and what is yours to supply?"

1.7 Reflection: "If you audited your last leadership review against the ACE-IT behaviours — where would you find the biggest gap between the ideal and the observable? What one behavioural change would create the most impact?"

§2. Say what the reflections are for.
Point learners to the portal section that they will be required to complete with as much depth as possible.
The reflections build the learning portfolio they receive at the end of the programme.

Say: "You write these reflections on the portal after the teaching, with as much depth as you can."

§3. Set the standard.
Say: "For 1.4, write the Shift, the Stake and the Step in the words your people would use.
For 1.5 and 1.7, name the observable evidence.
For 1.6, say which STAT element is missing and what is yours to supply."
Watch for: resistance named with no trigger. Ask: "Which of the five triggers is live?"

§4. Bridge to Section 2.
Say: "We know what alignment is and what a change must pass. Section 2 shows why this decides execution outcomes."

§ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
Participants write these four reflections in Section 1 of the participant file, at the foot of parts 1.4, 1.5, 1.6 and 1.7.

pictures.alt: 1.4 Reflection — The 3S Check: Write the Shift, the Stake and the Step for the change you are carrying through this unit. Which of the three would your people find hardest to say back, and why?

1.5 Reflection: Which SCARF trigger is most frequently activated in your organisation during strategy implementation? What is the observable evidence? What counter-strategy would address the root cause?

1.6 Reflection — The STAT Check: Run STAT for the change you are carrying through this unit. Which element is missing for the people it affects most? What is your evidence, and what is yours to supply?

1.7 Reflection: If you audited your last leadership review against the ACE-IT behaviours — where would you find the biggest gap between the ideal and the observable? What one behavioural change would create the most impact?

slides.title: Section 1 Reflections · 1.1 to 1.3
slides.notes:
§SECTION 1 REFLECTIONS · 1.1 TO 1.3

§HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:

§1. Show the slide and read the prompts aloud.
1.1 Reflection: "In your current role, which filter (Mind or Heart) tends to shape your first response to a new strategic priority? What are the implications?"

1.2 Reflection: "Which of the Five Principles describes the most critical gap in your leadership team right now? What is the evidence for this?"

1.3 Reflection — The event and the transition: "Write down one change your strategy requires of a named group. You will carry this change through the rest of the unit. On the day it was announced, how far through their own transition were the leaders, and how far were the people affected?"

§2. Say what the reflections are for.
Point learners to the portal section that they will be required to complete with as much depth as possible.
The reflections build the learning portfolio they receive at the end of the programme.

Say: "You write these reflections on the portal after the teaching, with as much depth as you can."

§3. Set the standard.
Say: "For 1.1 and 1.2, give the evidence: what you saw or heard. For 1.3, name the change, the group and the date."
Watch for: a change with no named group. Ask: "Whose Monday morning changes?"

§4. Say that four more follow.
Say: "The next slide holds the reflections on the four tools."

§ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
Participants write these three reflections in Section 1 of the participant file, at the foot of parts 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3.

pictures.alt: 1.1 Reflection: In your current role, which filter (Mind or Heart) tends to shape your first response to a new strategic priority? What are the implications?
1.2 Reflection: Which of the Five Principles describes the most critical gap in your leadership team right now? What is the evidence for this?

1.3 Reflection — The event and the transition: Write down one change your strategy requires of a named group. You will carry this change through the rest of the unit. On the day it was announced, how far through their own transition were the leaders, and how far were the people affected?

slides.title: Section 2 Reflections
slides.after: 2.3 · Why Change Must Be Led: Installed and Adopted
slides.notes:
§SECTION 2 REFLECTIONS

§HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:

§1. Show the slide and read the prompts aloud.
2.1 Reflection: "Think of a time when you personally chose to go beyond compliance and genuinely committed to a strategic direction. What caused that shift? What would it take to create that same shift in your team?"

2.2 Reflection: "How much of your current leadership time is spent enforcing compliance? What is the opportunity cost of this?"

2.3 Reflection — Installed and adopted: "Name one change in your organisation that is installed and still awaiting adoption. Which check did it fail: Mind, Heart, Hands or Habit? What has the adoption gap cost so far?"

§2. Say what the reflections are for.
Point learners to the portal section that they will be required to complete with as much depth as possible.
The reflections build the learning portfolio they receive at the end of the programme.

Say: "You write these reflections on the portal after the teaching, with as much depth as you can."

§3. Set the standard.
Say: "For 2.1, name the moment and what caused it.
For 2.2, give a share of your week and what it displaces.
For 2.3, name the change, the check it failed and a figure for the cost."
Watch for: a cost stated as a feeling. Ask: "What did it cost in rework, supervision or lost benefit?"

§4. Bridge to Section 3.
Say: "We know why alignment decides execution. Section 3 asks where in your organisation it is most at risk."

§ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
Participants write these three reflections in Section 2 of the participant file, at the foot of parts 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3.

pictures.alt: 2.1 Reflection: Think of a time when you personally chose to go beyond compliance and genuinely committed to a strategic direction. What caused that shift? What would it take to create that same shift in your team?
2.2 Reflection: How much of your current leadership time is spent enforcing compliance? What is the opportunity cost of this?

2.3 Reflection — Installed and adopted: Name one change in your organisation that is installed and still awaiting adoption. Which check did it fail: Mind, Heart, Hands or Habit? What has the adoption gap cost so far?

slides.title: Section 3 Reflections
slides.notes:
§SECTION 3 REFLECTIONS

§HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:

§1. Show the slide and read the prompts aloud.
3.1 Reflection — COMPASS Diagnostic: "Write your seven ratings. Which domain did you rate highest risk? What is the observable evidence? Is it still a High Flammable or has it crossed to Burning Platform?"

3.3 Reflection — Readiness: "For the change you are carrying through this unit, list the groups it affects and rate each on the 4 Checks. Which group is least ready? Which check fails first, and what is your evidence?"

§2. Say what the reflections are for.
Point learners to the portal section that they will be required to complete with as much depth as possible.
The reflections build the learning portfolio they receive at the end of the programme.

Say: "You write these reflections on the portal after the teaching, with as much depth as you can."

§3. Set the standard.
Say: "For 3.1, write your seven ratings first, then the evidence for the highest.
For 3.3, name each group, rate each check and say which check fails first."
Watch for: an average score for a group. Ask: "Which check fails first for this group?"

§4. Bridge to Section 4.
Say: "We know where alignment is at risk. Section 4 shows how the leadership team holds it together."

§ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
Participants write these two reflections in Section 3 of the participant file, at the foot of parts 3.1 and 3.3.

pictures.alt: 3.1 Reflection — COMPASS Diagnostic: Write your seven ratings. Which domain did you rate highest risk? What is the observable evidence? Is it still a High Flammable or has it crossed to Burning Platform?

3.3 Reflection — Readiness: For the change you are carrying through this unit, list the groups it affects and rate each on the 4 Checks. Which group is least ready? Which check fails first, and what is your evidence?

slides.title: Section 4 Reflections
slides.notes:
§SECTION 4 REFLECTIONS

§HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:

§1. Show the slide and read the prompts aloud.
4.1 Reflection: "Which state is your organisation currently closer to? What is the single most important convergence you need to achieve before your next major strategy initiative?"

4.2 Reflection: "What is the most important alignment conversation you need to have with a closely adjacent role in the next 30 days? What would that conversation need to address?"

4.3 Reflection — One voice: "Choose one group in your organisation. List every change the leadership team is asking of it this quarter. How many are there? Which of the four commitments is weakest in your team today?"

§2. Say what the reflections are for.
Point learners to the portal section that they will be required to complete with as much depth as possible.
The reflections build the learning portfolio they receive at the end of the programme.

Say: "You write these reflections on the portal after the teaching, with as much depth as you can."

§3. Set the standard.
Say: "For 4.1, name the state and one convergence.
For 4.2, name the role and what the conversation must address.
For 4.3, count the changes and name the weakest commitment."
Watch for: a conversation with no named role. Ask: "Which role, and by when?"

§4. Bridge to Section 5.
Say: "We have the checks, the hot zones and the commitments. Section 5 applies them to two changes your strategy requires."

§ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
Participants write these three reflections in Section 4 of the participant file, at the foot of parts 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3.

pictures.alt: 4.1 Reflection: Which state is your organisation currently closer to? What is the single most important convergence you need to achieve before your next major strategy initiative?
4.2 Reflection: What is the most important alignment conversation you need to have with a closely adjacent role in the next 30 days? What would that conversation need to address?

4.3 Reflection — One voice: Choose one group in your organisation. List every change the leadership team is asking of it this quarter. How many are there? Which of the four commitments is weakest in your team today?
